findings.title: Loose Python equality does not prove preservation of original nested native types
findings.detail: Unknown affected future_blob and the complete level2 record are compared using dict/list ==. Python accepts True for int1 and False for int0, and int0 for False. Native JSON also erases distinctions such as String versus StringName inside raw progress. The authenticated whole-record semantics SHA binds each snapshot to its own CFG/journal, but no preserved native subtree canonical/type comparison joins the original seed to the later changed progress record. Thus type drift in an unknown subtree or other record can pass.

findings.title: Expected retained filenames are not bound to their actual decoded revisions
findings.detail: records() verifies that filenames equal generation-1/generation but uses entry.revision independently for envelope verification. After all historical revisions are available, valid known g11/g12 raw documents can be replayed under g13/g14 filenames while a separately supplied known headSHA14 passes. The native GD verifies name against _verified revision, but the host does not repeat that binding.
